page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a burstable, budget-oriented server instance belonging to the g1 family. It features a shared physical core configuration with 1 vCPU running on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.7 GB of memory per core. It does not include any local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and ships with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the g1-small in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 1076.89, reflecting its shared-core architecture. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only small block cached operations reaching 80.25 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write operations drop to 10.49 GB/sec and 8.91 GB/sec respectively. Passmark metrics further confirm this profile, with a CPU score of 1263.03 and a database operations score of 564.91.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest resource footprint, the g1-small is highly cost-efficient for low-intensity workloads but presents clear performance tradeoffs. It is suited for lightweight tasks such as basic static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 0.54 GB/sec, or simple key-value caching with Redis SET operations performing at 0.59 million operations per second. It is not designed for resource-heavy database hosting, large-scale LLM inference, or multi-threaded compute tasks.
